newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Up to 400,000 Rwandans heading home - U.N. official.
newsitem.headline: Up to 400,000 Rwandans heading home - U.N. official.

text.p: Several hundred thousand Rwandan refugees were heading home from eastern Zaire on Friday, a United Nations official said.

"We have between 300,000 and 400,000 people on the move," Ray Wilkinson of the U.N. refugee agency told Reuters. "This is a very rough estimate. We got within five km (three miles) of the village of Sake which is around 20 km (12 miles) west of Mugunga. From this point back to Goma the road is completely blocked with moving refugees."
Wilkinson added that it was exteremely difficult to give a more accurate estimate of the number of people given the scale of the movement from Mugunga camp.

Brenda Barton, a spokeswoman for the World Food Programme in Gisenye in Rwanda, said an intial survey showed that there was "no food at all" in Mugunga camp, but water was not a problem. "We are seeing among the returning refugees a number of Zairean IDPs (internally displaced people) who are fleeing the fighting around Sake," she said.
"I could see a bottleneck occurring here in Rwanda because of the large numbers and because the Umubano camp is nearly full. Some of the people have bullet wounds," Barton said.
A strip of road some 30 km (20 miles) long between Goma and the outskirts of Sake was jammed solid with refugees. All refugees were moving back to Rwanda via the La Petite Barriere checkpoint.
